summary: Filter Records: applies a visual filter/sort/limit to an already-fetched array of records, client-side.
description: Filter Records narrows and orders an `items` array of records without touching the server: the filter, sorting and limit are configured on the node exactly like Query Records' visual filter, but evaluated locally against the incoming array. The result comes out on `items` with `count` alongside; `modified` fires when the output recomputes. Use `filter` (signal) to re-evaluate on demand and `enabled` to bypass.
whenToUse: Deriving multiple views from one fetched result set — tabs, local search-as-you-type, secondary sorts — without re-querying. When the full data set should never reach the client, filter in the query itself (Query Records) instead.

ports.items: Records in (input) and the filtered, sorted subset out (output).
ports.enabled: Boolean; when false the input passes through unfiltered.

runtimeBehavior: Filter-value inputs are generated from the visual filter you build in the editor (each 'value' placeholder becomes an input port) — runtime-discovered + editor-adapter, same mechanism as Query Records.
patterns: One Query Records fanned into several Filter Records: one fetch, many live views.
antiPatterns: Client-filtering an unlimited query as a substitute for server-side where/limit — the full class still crosses the network.
